title: IBM's breach report puts agent identity controls at the top of the checklist
friendlyTitle: AI agents need their own secure identities and limited access
summary: IBM and the Ponemon Institute's 2026 Cost of a Data Breach report says AI-driven attacks are growing as organizations expand agent use. IBM recommends identity-based runtime controls, tightly scoped permissions, human attribution, auditability, data discovery, and continuous monitoring.
friendlySummary: IBM says companies should control each agent's identity, permissions, data access, and activity logs as AI-related attacks grow.
whyItMatters: Organizations do not need exotic defenses before getting the basics right. Treat every agent as a separate operational identity, limit what it can read and do, and keep logs that connect actions to accountable humans.
friendlyWhyItMatters: An agent should not have a master key. Small permissions and clear logs make AI safer at work.
